newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks push higher at close, seen choppy.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks push higher at close, seen choppy.

text.p: Argentine stocks emerged from a selling wave Thursday and closed at session highs, relieved by a bounceback in the Mexican peso, dealers said.
But the outlook for Friday remained difficult to call.

"The market staged a technical bounce today although everyone's still pretty cautious," said Jorge Bonanno at traders Interfin. "Low volumes show people may stay on the defensive until the political row over corruption subsides."
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 1.6 percent to 569.72, after shedding more than 3.0 percent in the previous two sessions.
Traders said the bolsa was also favored by a surge on Wall Street on the back of good corporate results and a fresh batch of economic indicators showing moderate growth.
"The market is more or less steady, but it could still slip to technical support at 540 before making a lasting recovery," said one chart analyst.

After seven straight weeks of gains, stocks pulled back this week when government officials locked horns with former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo over corruption cover-up charges. Cavallo accused two ministers of meddling in court probes and manipulating judges.

In the session floor volume slowed to 16.2 million pesos from 19 million Wednesday. But over-the-counter turnover swelled to 144.7 million pesos from 125.7 million Wednesday, largely on options settlements.
The broad market index tacked on 1.3 percent, with winners pounding losers 40 to seven and 20 issues closing flat.

The day's best main-tier performers were steelmaker Acindar, which surged 4.5 percent, carmakers Sevel and Ciadea, which both jumped 3.3 percent, and petrochemical concern Ipako and footwear and textile firm Alpargatas, both up 2.9 percent.
The only MerVal losers were real estate developer Irsa and pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which dropped 1.9 percent and 0.5 percent, respectively.

Telefonica and Telecom, which took a drubbing with losses of more than 5.0 percent Wednesday on the back of an earnings estimate downgrade by UBS Securities, recovered 1.7 percent and 0.5 percent, respectively.
